newsitem.title: USA: UAL's United Air May load factor off.
newsitem.headline: UAL's United Air May load factor off.

text.p: UAL Corp said its United Airlines posted a total passenger load factor in May of 71.5 percent, down from 71.6 percent a year ago.

North American passenger load factor in the month rose 0.2 percentage points to 71.2 percent, while the Atlantic load factor gained 1.5 points to 85.5 percent and Latin American load factor rose 4.1 points to 59.7 percent. Pacific load factor in the month, however, dropped 3.3 points to 68.9 percent.
Total revenue passenger miles from scheduled service rose 3.1 percent to 10.04 billion in May. That included North American passenger miles of 6.22 billion, an increase of 1.7 percent.

"United's traffic in May continued a trend of modest growth in revenue passenger miles tracking a modest increase in seat capacity," John Edwardson, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement. "A particular bright spot was our increased efficiency in our Latin American markets where traffic rose 5.2 percent while seat capacity was reduced 2.0 percent. This translated into a 4.1 percent jump in the passenger load factor to 59.7 percent."
Total revenue passenger miles including charter flights rose 3.1 percent to 10.05 billion in May.
Total scheduled available seat miles were 14,044,172,000, up 3.3 percent from 13,602,046,000 a year ago.
Total cargo ton miles for May were 237,935,000, up 19.5 percent from 199,066,000 a year ago.
Year-to-date passenger load factor gained 0.7 percentage points to 70.3 percent from 69.6 percent.
